lenses_summary.verification_red_team: Chosen idea rests on primary pages read tonight: Oura official blog (no-AI, 35 modelmakers, 3 weeks), Gartner release (n=1,539 US, Oct 2025), Campaign/Sprout Social numbers. Risks: Gartner is stated preference in one country; Sprout sentiment is social chatter, not sales; Etsy percentages unverified and must not be used; Famous Campaigns is opinion. Do not claim 'handmade sells more'; claim 'effort is read as care' as the strategist's interpretation (costly-signal idea), labelled as opinion.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Effort heuristic: people value what they believe took effort; costly signals are believed because they are hard to fake. In an AI-saturated feed, 68% wonder whether content is real, so visible human effort becomes a trust shortcut. Business owners feel the tension directly: AI makes their content cheaper and faster, and the reel asks what that cheapness tells customers. Strong for both Persian- and English-speaking owners.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Fits Behnood's voice (strategist and designer, craft, monochrome object style): the topic literally argues for the kind of considered work he does. Commercial: positions him as the person who knows where to spend effort. Not anti-technology preaching: framing is 'spend effort where the customer can see it', not 'never use AI'.

gates.brand_fit: pass: C01-C05 cluster, C06, C10; fail/defer: C07 (thin), C09 (overlap 10-24), C11 (overlap 10-25, unread)
gates.story: C01 cluster wins: tension (the cheaper you make it, the less it is believed) plus the most concrete image (35 people hand-building a tiny city for three weeks to sell a ring). C06 runner-up: clean naming story, but weaker image for an international audience.

decision.why: Strongest tension and most concrete image; works for Persian and English business audiences; evergreen idea (effort as a signal) with a fresh spark (Oura, Christmas ad season).
